document.title: Lower Bounds on the Overhead of Indistinguishability Obfuscation

candidate.title: Obfuscation Overhead for Single-Output Circuits
candidate.subtitle: Proved for multi-output circuits; blocked on the NP-hardness of single-output circuit minimization
candidate.one_line: Under NP not in BPP, no efficient iO scheme for single-output circuits of size s outputs circuits of size s + o(s/log s).
candidate.status_note: The first of the source's named main open problems. Its main theorem gives an Omega(s/log s) additive overhead lower bound for multi-output circuits under NP not in BPP, an assumption that is minimal since a zero-overhead iO scheme exists if NP is in BPP. The single-output case is not covered.
candidate.progress_note: The route runs through NP-hardness of a gap version of Multi-MCSP under randomized approximate Levin reductions, extending Ilango-Loff-Oliveira. The single-output analogue would be a step toward NP-hardness of MCSP, which the source calls a challenging open problem. The source does prove a single-output result in the database-aided model.

parameters.meaning: circuit size, counted as AND/OR/NOT gates
output size of the obfuscator; the ruled-out target is s + o(s/log s)

candidate.why_interesting: An overhead lower bound under the weakest possible assumption, whose extension to the standard single-output setting is blocked on a named decades-old open problem.
candidate.why_clean: One primitive, one size measure, one additive bound.

check.notes: The source names the direction without restating the bound, so the specific form -- same s + o(s/log s) target, same NP not in BPP assumption -- is this statement's choice and is flagged as such. Four page claims were corrected by grounding: the single-output remark is on page 5 not 8, the MCSP obstruction and the padding argument on page 8 not 9, and the bottleneck remark on page 33 not 32. The statement separates two things easy to conflate: the padding from arbitrary multi-output shapes to the square case is solved, while the drop to one output bit is not.
